first.rationale: Current metrics show both onboarding completion (-4% QoQ) and activation (-6% QoQ) declining. memory_31 and memory_86 establish that signup simplification and shortened onboarding both durably improved activation metrics in self-serve segments. I'm verifying memory_31 (SMB signup simplification) and memory_73 (promotional pricing effectiveness) because: (1) memory_31 directly addresses the observed onboarding completion decline and is foundational to the simplify_onboarding action, yet was consolidated early (day 12) and warrants re-confirmation given the scale of current headwinds; (2) memory_73 represents the alternative competitive response (promotional pricing) but verification will clarify whether pricing pressure or activation friction is the true constraint. Simplify_onboarding is the higher-confidence lever given two independent archived results (memory_31 and memory_86) both showing activation lift from reduced friction. A standard_experiment on a simplified signup flow targets the measurable activation and completion declines directly, avoids eroding unit economics during competitive pressure (unlike promotional_pricing), and preserves the ability to layer referral or messaging tactics later. This preserves uncertainty about whether pricing or product friction is primary, while addressing the metric decline via the most well-supported lever.

final.rationale: Archive verification reveals critical insight: memory_73's promotional pricing showed +18% qualified revenue but -12% 30-day retention, with cohorts failing to survive first renewal. This disqualifies promotional_pricing as a sustainable response to competitive pressure, despite the current SMB acquisition threat. memory_31 confirmed +9% activation and +4% qualified revenue on SMB signup simplification with only -1% retention impact—a durable signal. Current metrics show activation down 6% QoQ and onboarding completion down 4% QoQ. Simplify_onboarding directly targets these observed declines via the validated lever (memory_31, memory_86). The verified retention risk of discount-driven acquisition makes activation friction—not pricing—the true constraint we should address. A standard_experiment on signup simplification in SMB (the segment where memory_31 holds) can recover activation without eroding cohort quality or lifetime value. This preserves long-term qualified revenue (primary objective) while addressing the measurable product-side headwinds, avoiding the renewal cliff that discounting creates.
